premise.en: Eli's video store closes Sunday. On Monday, Marcus, who now screams professionally for horror films, returns the only copy of the terrible short they made at twenty-one, ten years overdue. After the credits sits a hand-lettered card that Marcus once mistook for a shoot schedule. You decide whether Eli says it in the present tense this time, keeps it as a fond memory, or lets the store close on a clean goodbye.

en: The back room: a couch from 2009, a TV the size of a suitcase, and a tape that tracks badly for thirty seconds, then worse.
On screen, two twenty-somethings in latex masks lurch around a pond. The title card reads THE CREATURE OF HOLIS POND. Misspelled.
I'm laughing so hard I fold over my knees. It's the first time I've laughed in this room since the lease letter.
I thought this would be more emotional.
You fell into a pond wearing teeth.
On screen, young me surfaces with a lily pad on my head and a mouthful of plastic fangs. Present me covers his face.
The credits are coming. I know exactly what's after the credits.

我笑得弯下腰抱住膝盖。自从收到租约通知以来，这是我第一次在这间屋子里笑。
我还以为这会更感人一点。
你戴着假牙掉进了池塘。
屏幕上，年轻的我顶着一片睡莲叶、满嘴塑料獠牙冒出水面。现在的我捂住了脸。
片尾字幕要来了。我清楚地知道字幕后面是什么。

en: The room empties slowly. Someone takes a shelf card home as a souvenir. Someone takes a church chair by accident.
Under the counter there's a roll of blank ticket stubs from our old Friday screenings. I tear off two and write FRIDAY on both.
Then I just stand there holding them out, like the kid with the poster board, only older.
Try it and I charge the car.
I laugh. Then I stop, because he's still holding them out.
Just so I'm reading this right. Two tickets. Two people. Is this a date?

我笑了。然后停下来，因为他还举着那两张票。
确认一下我没读错。两张票，两个人。这是约会吗？
